conflict_synopsis.core_view: Canada 5Y is historically rich versus the US on a cyclically warmer Canada with a live BoC energy pass-through trigger, so the CA-US 5Y spread should converge higher after a fully priced Fed hike.
conflict_synopsis.key_catalyst: BoC pass-through communication or Canada data after a delivered, already-priced Fed hike.
conflict_synopsis.key_invalidation: BoC takes pass-through off the table while Canada temperatures fall below the US, or a new common-date CA-US 5Y extreme from further US-led selloff.

remit: historical or fundamental dislocations and convergence trades
stance_summary: CA-US 5Y at a historical cheap-Canada extreme is a peer-spread dislocation, not a weak-Canada story: Canada activity and consumer temperatures sit above the US, the Fed hike is already delivered into 99th-percentile US yields, and BoC minutes keep energy pass-through as the live tightening trigger while Bank Rate is still 2.25%. Own it in duration-matched 5Y rates RV, not USDCAD.

catalysts: Next BoC minutes, testimony, or CPI print that keeps headline energy pass-through alive versus core still near 2%.
Global tightening impulse (delivered Fed hike, BoJ to 1.25%, BoE 6-3 hold with QT) keeping the US from being the only hawkish curve.
Canada activity remaining above-US while US consumer temperature stays at 48.5, forcing the 5Y peer gap to re-normalize rather than trend further cheap.
evidence_refs: rollup:BoC minutes flag higher energy pass-through risk
rollup:Canada August inflation holds at 3%, core stays near 2%

expression_comparison.rates_candidate: Pay CA 5Y vs receive US 5Y (long the CA minus US 5Y sovereign spread) using the common-date packet print of -124bp as of 2026-09-17.
expression_comparison.rationale: The mispricing lives in the 5Y peer spread: CA-US 5Y is a |z|>=2 opportunity-sample extreme at 0th percentile and -124bp, whereas USDCAD is only 87th percentile 5y with z_5y 0.99. The packet USDCAD vs CA-US_2Y residual is weak (r-squared 0.022), so spot does not own the discrepancy. Two-year USD-CAD carry of 140bp supports receive-US/pay-CA and opposes short USDCAD. NZ official yields are unavailable, so NZ-involved rates RV is out. Rates RV is therefore the cleaner, carry-supported expression; spot is the inferior alternative, not the selected trade.
expression_comparison.spot_candidate: Short USDCAD (CAD higher versus USD) as the FX expression of CA-US policy-gap compression.

trade.horizon: 1-3 months, through the next BoC communication and Canada inflation/activity prints after the delivered FOMC hike
trade.invalidation: BoC communication that energy pass-through is contained while Canada activity and consumer temperatures fall below the US, or a new common-date CA-US 5Y extreme driven by further US-led selloff after the already-delivered hike. Right-thesis/wrong-timing if the spread stays cheap without those falsifiers.
trade.mispricing: Canada 5Y is historically rich versus US 5Y (CA-US 5Y at the bottom of the 1y distribution and a |z|>=2 opportunity extreme) while Canada's activity/consumer temperatures are above the US and BoC policy is still 2.25% against a delivered Fed 3.75-4.00% band. That is a peer-relationship dislocation, not a justified weak-Canada discount.
principal_risks: Saudi Oman workaround reduced the extreme oil-supply tail and oil eased modestly; if that kills BoC pass-through, Canada can stay rich versus the US.
Canada core is already near target (CPI-trim 1.9%, CPI-median 2.0%), so headline 3% alone may not force a hike from 2.25%.
US 5Y rose 8bp on 2026-09-18 after the -124bp common-date print; continued US-led selloff without a Canada print would cheapen the spread further.
No positioning/flow dataset; crowding of long-US versus short-Canada duration is unknown.
Executable broker prices are not in the packet; levels stay null.
trade.structure: Duration-matched cross-market 5Y rates RV: pay Canadian 5Y sovereign, receive US 5Y Treasury.
trade.thesis: Verified fact: on common dates the packet prints CA-US 5Y at -124bp as of 2026-09-17, 1y percentile 0.20, 5y percentile 6.94, z_1y -2.03; the opportunity monitor flags the same series at percentile 0.0 and z -2.05. CA 5Y is 3.54% and CA 2Y 3.27% as of 2026-09-17; US 5Y is 4.86% and US 2Y 4.76% as of 2026-09-18, so the US legs are one session newer. CA-US 2Y is -140bp (1y percentile 3.77, 5y percentile 4.30). Fed funds are 3.75-4.00% after a delivered 25bp hike that futures had priced at greater-than-90% going in; BoC held at 2.25% and named broader energy pass-through as the conditional tightening trigger. Canada August headline CPI is 3.0% y/y with CPI-trim 1.9% and CPI-median 2.0%; US inflation temperature is 52.0 versus CA 50.0. Canada activity 53.2 and consumer 52.5 sit above US activity 49.92 and consumer 48.5; CA Q2 real GDP was +0.8% q/q. Inference: a 124bp 5Y cheap-Canada gap versus the US is not the right peer price for a cyclically warmer Canada with a still-live BoC pass-through trigger. The valuation anchor is the common-date 5Y spread against its 1y/5y distribution plus comparable-country temperatures, not the fact that Canada yields failed to keep up with the post-CPI US selloff. Convergence should begin now because the US hike is behind the market and already in extreme US yield percentiles, while the next relative-policy increment is Canada's reaction function, not another fully priced FOMC step. Two closing channels both raise CA-US 5Y: Canada yields catch up, or stretched US yields cheapen more than Canada. Unknown: executable broker levels; Canada's 2026-09-18 common-date print after the US 5Y +8bp session; whether pass-through actually forces BoC action; positioning.
why_now: The Fed 25bp hike is delivered and had been greater-than-90% priced; US 2Y/5Y/10Y sit at 99th-100th percentiles on the opportunity sample, so incremental US hawkish news is largely in the US legs.

CA-US 5Y is already a 0th-percentile / z about -2.05 extreme and widened 12bp over five sessions (5d move z -2.03) into the post-FOMC window, which is when relative-policy convergence typically starts.

BoC minutes just kept energy pass-through as the conditional hike trigger while Bank Rate remains 2.25%, and the desk thesis is that the energy shock is constraining global easing even where growth is softer.
Canada activity 53.2 and consumer 52.5 versus US 49.92 and 48.5 falsify the idea that the cheap CA-US 5Y is simply a weaker Canadian cycle.
